MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Eligibility will be based upon a clear showing the applicant has education, training, and experience of the scope and quality sufficient to effectively carry-out the duties of the position. Candidates must exemplify the corporate perspective, leadership vision, broad experience and character needed in the SES corps not only to satisfy the immediate vacancy, but future vacancies which will occur in a variety of organizations, functions and locations. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. In accordance with new OPM requirements to streamline Senior Executive Service (SES) hiring, applicants are no longer required to submit lengthy narrative essays, including those for Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or Mandatory Technical Qualifications (TQs), when applying. Instead, the initial application will be resume-only, capped at two pages. This change streamlines the application process and more closely aligns with private industry practices. Applicants identified for potential selection will have their ECQs assessed by undergoing a structured interview with the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Review Board (QRB). To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the education, Technical Qualifications (TQ), and Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) related to this position within your resume (not to exceed 2 pages). Resumes over the 2-page limit will be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. CERTIFICATIONS: Level III APDP Program Management TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that satisfy the technical qualifications. TQ1: Demonstrated expertise in leading enterprise-level PPBE execution, overseeing multi-billion-dollar RDT&E and procurement portfolios, and ensuring resources are aligned to support rapid capability delivery. Proven ability to direct cost, schedule, and performance reporting for senior leadership and to manage Special Access Program governance across diverse mission areas. Extensive experience developing, codifying, and implementing acquisition policies and procedures and managing enterprise acquisition review forums that enable timely decisions for development, production, and fielding. TQ2: Exceptional capability in leading enterprise integration, acquisition policy development, and stakeholder alignment across headquarters, field commands, and interagency partners. Demonstrated success in building and directing cross-functional teams responsible for policy development, PPBE execution, SAP oversight, and strategic integration. Recognized for fostering collaborative relationships, ensuring stakeholder perspectives are accurately represented in senior decision forums, and shaping organizational structures and workforce competencies that strengthen long-term space acquisition integration. TQ3: Superior qualifications in providing senior advisory support on acquisition programs, legislative matters, and enterprise strategy. Extensive experience preparing senior officials for Congressional testimony, developing responses to Congressional inquiries, and maintaining effective relationships with Members of Congress and staff. Proven ability to represent senior leadership in engagements with OSW, military departments, industry, GAO, foreign partners, and other stakeholders. Demonstrated skill in developing SAP legislative strategies, resolving complex policy issues, and supporting crisis planning and exercises outside normal duty hours. TQ4: Advanced proficiency in leading large, technically complex acquisition organizations and shaping enterprise strategy, workforce development, and organizational performance. Holds Level III APDP Program Management certification and possesses extensive experience managing major defense acquisition programs, including international and multi-agency efforts. Demonstrated ability to develop acquisition talent pipelines, strengthen organizational processes, and implement structures that support long-term integration across the space acquisition enterprise. Recognized for disciplined execution, strategic foresight, and continuous improvement in delivering mission-critical space capabilities. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): All new appointees to the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the five mandatory ECQs: ECQ 1. Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding: Demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2. Driving Efficiency: Demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3. Merit and Competence: Demonstrated knowledge, ability, and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4. Leading People: Demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5. Achieving Results: Demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Please note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program, or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you must attach proof (e.g., SF-50 or Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.

Details.JobSummary: Click on "Learn more about this agency" button below for IMPORTANT additional information. This position, situated within the Office of the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Space Acquisition and Integration (SAF/SQ), plays a critical national security role by driving the policy, planning, and performance metrics necessary to deliver integrated space capabilities across the Department of War.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Space Acquisition and Integration (SAF/SQ)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is to fly, fight and win...airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Reach and Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do.
MajorDuties: The role oversees all financial, policy, and legislative activities for Space Force acquisitions, acting as a critical bridge between senior leadership, Congress, and Department of War stakeholders to ensure the rapid and effective delivery of space capabilities. The incumbent leads enterprise-level oversight of Space Force investment funding, managing Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) actions to ensure resources continuously support program execution and the rapid fielding of capabilities. This comprehensive oversight includes directing cost, schedule, and performance reporting, as well as managing Special Access Program (SAP) governance across the Department of War. To maintain portfolio health, the executive develops, codifies, and enforces space acquisition policies while supervising the acquisition review forums necessary for the Space Service Acquisition Executive to make critical development and production decisions. Beyond program and financial oversight, the position is responsible for driving enterprise integration and stakeholder alignment. The incumbent builds and leads teams focused on policy development and SAP oversight, fostering deep collaborative relationships across the Space Force Staff, Air Staff, Field Commands, and other DoW organizations. A core duty is ensuring that diverse stakeholder views are accurately synthesized and communicated to executive decision-makers, while simultaneously cultivating the personnel skills and organizational structures required for long-term space acquisition success. Furthermore, the executive serves as a senior advisor and primary external representative, providing technical assistance to the Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary for Congressional testimonies and inquiries. The incumbent maintains active liaisons with lawmakers and represents leadership in negotiations with the Office of the Secretary of War (OSW), other military departments, industry partners, foreign governments, and the Government Accountability Office (GAO). By formulating strategic policies and leading SAP legislative engagement, the executive works to build consensus, resolve cross-organizational conflicts, and support crisis management efforts.
Details.Education: A master's degree in appropriate professional or administrative discipline and an advanced degree in a related business or management field is highly desirable. Certification Required: Level III APDP Program Management
Details.Evaluations: Once the application process is complete, a review of your resume and supporting documentation will be conducted. If you meet the education, eligibility, and minimum qualifications requirements, your Application Package will be further reviewed to determine if you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) and Technical Qualifications (TQ) listed above. ECQs and TQs must be thoroughly addressed within your two (2) page resume. Separate narratives will not be accepted or reviewed. Applicants will be evaluated against the qualifications requirements by a screening panel composed of senior executives and/or general officers selected for organizational and/or functional backgrounds relevant to this position. Highly Qualified applicants may undergo one or more interviews and may be referred to the selecting official for further consideration. Final selection is contingent on approval by the Secretary of the Air Force. Upon selection, if not already a member of the SES serving under a career appointment, the selected candidate must have their executive qualifications certified by the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Review Board (QRB) prior to appointment. The selected candidate's application will be forwarded to OPM for review and certification by the QRB, unless the selectee provides evidence of their noncompetitive status (i.e., a current SES, OPM QRB certified SESCDP graduate, or SES reinstatement eligible). Once QRB certified, the selected candidates will be required to serve a one-year probationary period. For more information regarding the SES, please visit: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/senior-executive-service/.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Conditions of Employment: Position is designated Special Sensitive and requires eligibility for access to Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI), other intelligence-related Special Sensitive information, or involvement in Top Secret Special Access Programs (SAP) to fully perform the duties and responsibilities of the position. A non-disclosure agreement must be signed. This position has been designated by the Air Force as a Testing Designated Position (TDP) under the Air Force Civilian Drug Demand Reduction Program. Employee must pass initial and periodic short notice drug testing. Illegal drug use by employees in sensitive positions presents a clear threat to the mission of the Air Force, national security, and public safety. In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions- Management and Program Analysis (0343) SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-12, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes mastery of advanced management, organizational principles, and qualitative/quantitative analytical methods to serve as an authoritative expert in evaluating the efficiency, effectiveness, and strategic alignment of CWMD program operations. Expert knowledge of Department of the Air Force, OSD, Joint Staff, and interagency CWMD/CBRN defense policies, program objectives, and operational planning frameworks across multiple echelons. Expert-level mastery in applying specialized operational modeling tools and risk calculation systems (including HPAC, VLSTRACK, RAPTOR, Sortie Generation calculators, and Dry Filter Unit [DFU] siting models) to translate raw scientific data and adversary threat capabilities into measurable mission impacts. Comprehensive knowledge required to analyze, evaluate, and determine the operational benefit, strengths, and limitations of specialized equipment and materiel/non-materiel solutions (such as evaluating aircrew CBRN-protective flight suit modifications and Contamination Control Point workflows). FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-12 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-13 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge and background of Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction (CWMD) and CBRN defense principles, policies, to identify relevant factors for executing and sustaining Air Force missions in contaminated environments. (e.g., factors necessary to enable or expand sortie generation, and/or threat factor that hinder sortie generation). Skill in qualitative and quantitative analysis to effectively gather, assemble, parse, and scrutinize relevant facts to successfully weigh issues, draw conclusions, conduct analysis, and devise recommended solutions; this is to support sortie generation, installation attack response, provide command and control, recommend proper mission oriented protective posture and other CBRN-related operational missions, to accomplish DAF objectives in CBRN hazard environments. Skill in independently engaging in complex projects, while negotiating difficult issues across diverse military and civilian staffs, as well as demonstrating the ability to inform operational guidance development to advance DAF organizational equities. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, translating highly technical issues into understandable principles that make persuasive arguments, maintain good working relationships, effectively informs executive leadership, and advances DAF mission equities PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MajorDuties: The primary purpose of this position is: to serve as an Air Force Program Analyst within the HQ AF/A10 Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction (CWMD) Division, executing strategic, multi-disciplinary program evaluation and analytical support. The incumbent evaluates, validates, and refines Department of the Air Force CWMD policies, strategies, and operational plans to ensure maximum program effectiveness, while collaborating across Joint Staff, sister Services, and OSD echelons to secure vital DAF warfighting equities in CBRN-contested environments. Duties: Conducts comprehensive CWMD and CBRN operational analyses to inform and shape AF CWMD policy, strategies, CONOPs, program effectiveness. Researches and evaluates Air Force CWMD policies, analytic products, materiel and non-materiel solutions to resolve critical operational vulnerabilities, improving operational efficiency. Defines complex operational issues, synthesizes multi-source data, and determines the most effective and efficient method and approach to fulfill organizational tasks, resource requirements, and long-term program objectives. Develops recommended CWMD Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs), handbooks, science-based Operational Risk Management (ORM) decision aids, and operational guidance documents, and other products that address the employment of materiel and personnel in "CBRN-contested" environments.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the Pentagon Force Protection Agency (PFPA) is to provide force protection, security, and law enforcement to safeguard personnel, facilities, infrastructure, and other resources for the Pentagon Reservation and designated Department of War (DoW) facilities (hereinafter referred to as "the Pentagon Facilities") within the National Capital Region (NCR). PFPA addresses the full spectrum of threats by utilizing a balanced approach of comprehensive protective intelligence and counterintelligence analysis, to include forensic and biometric-enabled information, to determine the appropriate protective posture for personnel and facilities; prevention, preparedness, detection; all-hazards response; DoW emergency management; support the lead response management agency during an emergency or crisis; and provide comprehensive threat assessments, security, and protection services for Office of the Secretary of War personnel and other persons. The PFPA is the DoW focal point for collaborating and coordinating with other DoW Components, other Executive departments and agencies, and State and local authorities on matters involving force protection, security, and law enforcement activities that impact the Pentagon Facilities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: The employee makes recommendations on the creative use of non-print media to reach a wide range of audiences. The employee drafts: speeches, remarks, talking points, statements, graphics and other related documents for the PFPA Director and Deputy Director. The employee identifies opportunities for planning and executing communication events, nationwide, to spotlight PFPA's programs. Oversees all arrangements with the news media involving PFPA activities.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: IMPORTANT INFORMATION: This Job Opportunity Announcement (JOA) will be used to form a pool of qualified applicants who will be considered for direct hire vacancies as they become available. To learn more about the United States Space Force Mission click here
MajorDuties: The United States Space Force (USSF) HQ at the Pentagon is searching for a Corporate Processes and Governance Lead to support HQSF S/3/4/7 (NH-0343-04, GS-14/15 Equivalent). Description: Serve at Headquarters United States Space Force in the Pentagon as the Corporate Processes and Governance Lead for the Office of the Deputy Chief of Space Operations for Operations, HQSF S3/4/7. Reporting to the Director of Staff, you will serve as the organization's principal functional lead for corporate workflow, knowledge management, governance, records-management integration, and business-process improvement. Within Director of Staff and senior-leader guidance, you will independently lead a high-visibility, organization-wide program supporting more than 230 personnel and advise the Director of Staff and senior leaders on the effectiveness, risks, and improvement of internal business operations. You will establish the strategy, governance framework, performance measures, and operating procedures for the HQSF S3/4/7 ETMS2 workflow and corporate-process portfolio. You will use data and organizational analysis to identify systemic barriers, improve decision and information flow, strengthen accountability, and implement approved process improvements across the headquarters. You will provide functional leadership and coordinate government requirements for a two-person contractor team supporting workflow operations, while focusing your own efforts on program direction, governance, senior-leader engagement, cross-functional integration, and continuous improvement. This position does not exercise formal supervisory authority over military or federal civilian personnel. Ideal Candidate: The ideal candidate will possess a bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education, training, and extensive, progressively responsible experience in management analysis, business operations, workflow management, knowledge management, governance, or related fields. The candidate will demonstrate expert-level ability to independently lead complex, enterprise-level programs; analyze organizational performance; develop governance and process-improvement strategies; and advise senior leaders on business operations, workflow, and organizational effectiveness. The candidate will have substantial experience with Enterprise Task Management Software Solution 2 (ETMS2), or comparable enterprise task-management systems, including tasker intake, routing, assignment, suspense management, status reporting, quality control, and executive-level visibility. Experience with Microsoft Teams, Planner, PowerBI, SharePoint, records-management practices, collaboration tools, process mapping, standard operating procedures, governance forums, performance metrics, and continuous process improvement is highly desired. The successful candidate will be an independent, organized, and proactive professional who can manage competing priorities; analyze organizational problems; develop practical and sustainable solutions; communicate effectively with senior leaders and action officers; and build productive working relationships across a large headquarters organization. The candidate will be able to translate Director of Staff and senior-leader priorities into sustainable organizational processes; lead cross-functional implementation efforts; and exercise sound independent judgment, consistent with established guidance and leadership intent, in resolving complex workflow, governance, and knowledge-management issues. Knowledge, Skills & Abilities: 1. In-depth understanding of strategic planning processes, including the ability to align organizational goals with strategic initiatives. 2. Comprehensive knowledge of organizational structure, functions, and interrelationships within a command environment. 3. Familiarity with military protocols, customs, and courtesies, as well as knowledge of military chain of command and operations. 4. Knowledge of legislative processes and the ability to coordinate with legislative bodies and respond to congressional inquiries. 5. Understanding of project management principles, including planning, execution, and monitoring of projects.

MajorDuties: Headquarters Space Force Mission Sustainment/Logistics Directorate (HQSF/S4O) at The Pentagon is searching for a Technical Director (NH-0343-04, GS-14/15 Equivalent). Description: Headquarters is seeking a dynamic and highly accomplished leader with deep expertise in strategic planning, resource governance, and organizational transformation to serve as the Technical Director. Operating in a high-operations-tempo, high-visibility environment, this individual strategically leads and supervises a multidisciplinary team of military officers, civil service personnel, and contractors, seamlessly translating senior leadership intent into coordinated, decisive action. The incumbent directs front-office operations and integrates strategic initiatives across the enterprise, establishing the structures, integrated communications, and synchronized battle rhythms necessary to execute mission priorities at scale. By combining exceptional technical credibility with sound operational discipline, this leader turns complex, cross-functional challenges into compelling, decision-ready products, overseeing special projects and managing resource governance to enable senior leaders to resolve critical issues proactively before they impact global mission execution. The Mission Sustainment/Logistics Directorate (S4O) is seeking a highly accomplished Supervisory Management and Program Analyst to serve as Technical Director, bringing a robust background in leading senior-level headquarters staff teams, strategic planning, policy development, and enterprise mission execution within the Department of War (DoW), with preferred command-level experience in the Space Force, Air Force, or broader defense enterprise. Academically, the ideal candidate will hold a bachelor's degree in business, public administration, organizational leadership, engineering management, national security studies, systems management, or a related field, with a master's degree strongly preferred. Professionally, this individual must demonstrate progressive senior leadership experience directing complex staff organizations, front-office operations, and integrated program portfolios, with a commanding track record of aligning organizational goals to executable initiatives, resolving systemic organizational friction, and leading high-performing military and civilian teams in fast-paced, high-visibility environments. Operating as a senior technical authority, the incumbent provides authoritative expertise across assigned Space Staff programs, identifies systemic operating problems, resolves conflicting priorities, and shapes strategic communications, high-level staff papers, and executive products to govern the executive battle rhythm and support senior leader decision-making. Requiring exceptional communication skills, sharp interpersonal judgment, adaptability, and the discretion to handle sensitive information, the successful candidate must be able to obtain and maintain a Top-Secret clearance with SCI eligibility, meet special-sensitive position requirements, and operate effectively under travel and unscheduled overtime demands. Knowledge Skills and Abilities: In-depth understanding of strategic planning processes, including the ability to align organizational goals with strategic initiatives. Comprehensive knowledge of organizational structure, functions, and interrelationships within a command environment. Familiarity with military protocols, customs, and courtesies, as well as knowledge of military chain of command and operations. Knowledge of legislative processes and the ability to coordinate with legislative bodies and respond to congressional inquiries. Understanding of project management principles, including planning, execution, and monitoring of projects. Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to prepare speeches, presentations, and official documents. Strong coordination skills to facilitate meetings, events, and strategic engagements. Analytical skills to assess and interpret data, develop plans, and ensure accurate information flow. Leadership skills to oversee and guide team activities, manage projects, and provide direction to staff. Effective problem-solving skills to address issues, find solutions, and implement changes as needed. Ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities simultaneously in a fast-paced environment. Ability to adapt to changing situations, handle unexpected challenges, and remain flexible in achieving objectives. Keen attention to detail to ensure accuracy and completeness in all tasks and communications. Strong interpersonal skills to build relationships, work collaboratively with diverse groups, and facilitate team efforts. Ability to handle sensitive information with discretion and maintain confidentiality at all times.

MajorDuties: Headquarters Space Force Mission Sustainment/Logistics Directorate (HQSF/S4O) at The Pentagon is searching for a Chief, Congressional Affairs (NH-0301-04, GS-14/15 Equivalent). Description: The Space Force Deputy for Installations and Logistics is seeking an accomplished leader with deep expertise in congressional affairs, legislative strategy, and defense policy to serve as the Congressional Chief and Senior Legislative Advisor. Operating in a high-tempo, high-visibility environment, this individual serves as the principal legislative authority for a diverse portfolio spanning installations, logistics, infrastructure, sustainment, military construction (MILCON), environmental programs, energy, and force protection. The successful candidate will strategically lead a multidisciplinary team of military, civilian, and contractor personnel to shape senior-level legislative positions while driving precise tactical execution on short-notice, high-sensitivity congressional actions. This leader oversees the full life cycle of inquiries, testimony preparation, hearing support, and formal responses, ensuring all communications are aligned and technically accurate. The ideal candidate will possess a robust background in congressional affairs, defense policy analysis, and headquarters-level staff operations within the Department of War (DoW), preferably with direct experience supporting Space Force, Air Force, or broader military portfolios in installations, logistics, or infrastructure. Educationally, this individual should hold a bachelor's degree in public policy, public administration, engineering, logistics, or a related field (advanced degree preferred). Professionally, this leader will bring progressive senior-level experience advising on legislative affairs, backed by hands-on experience on Capitol Hill and a track record of translating complex technical issues into clear products for senior leaders. A deep working knowledge of legislative formulation, statutory analysis, and the PPBE process is essential, along with a proven history of leading teams and developing high-impact executive correspondence. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities: Expert Knowledge of Space Force/DoW Installations, Engineering, and Logistics: Comprehensive, expert-level understanding of civil engineering, strategic basing, MILCON, real property management, environmental cleanup, utility operations, base realignment (BRAC), space weapon systems sustainment, and force protection/security forces policies and requirements. Knowledge of Legislative Formulation and Policy Analysis: Executive knowledge to formulate and coordinate organizational positions on pending legislation, analyze complex congressional bills, and evaluate the programmatic impact of statutory language. Expert Knowledge of Space Staff, Air Staff, and Secretariat Organizations: Deep, in-depth understanding of the missions, roles, functions, and interrelationships among the Space Staff (SF/S), Air Staff, Secretariat (SAF/IE, SAF/LL, SAF/FMBL), Joint Staff, and OSD. Mastery of the Congressional Budget Process and PPBE: Thorough, working knowledge of the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process, its direct linkages to the congressional budget cycle, and major defense authorizing and appropriating committees. Advanced Written Communication and Synthesis Skills: Demonstrated, high-level skill in researching, analyzing, and synthesizing complex technical and programmatic data into clear, executive-level products including skull slides, witness testimonies, QFRs, OSD Heartburn Appeals, and formal reports. Exceptional Oral Communication, Diplomacy, and Negotiation Skills: Mastery of verbal communication and presentation techniques to effectively brief senior executives, negotiate sensitive and controversial issues with legislative staffers, and build consensus among diverse agencies. Executive Management and Leadership Skills: Proven leadership and administrative ability to direct, plan, organize, mentor, and task a team of action officers and cross-functional working groups to execute high-stakes congressional requirements under tight, unpredictable deadlines. Ability to Independently Evaluate Program Effectiveness and Make Critical Decisions: Ability to analyze legislative changes to make sound independent judgments, assess long-term program impacts on resources, and defend complex, high-visibility decisions to senior Space Force leadership.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. All qualifications requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume. Your resume may not exceed two (2) pages. This "certification" must include your rank, dates of active duty service, type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable), and date any terminal leave will begin. Details.JobSummary: Located in the Washington Headquarters Services, Correspondence Analysis Branch (CAB), this position supports the Secretary of War and leadership. CAB oversees unclassified official correspondence, staff packages, military nominations, and CATMS records management for Department of War components. Note: This is an operational role requiring evening, weekend, and holiday coverage, with staff remaining "on call" during off-duty hours.
Details.SubAgencyName: Executive Services Directorate, Correspondence Management Division
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Washington Headquarters Services (WHS) is a world-class service organization, with a dynamic workforce and unwavering commitment to service excellence. WHS is the essential services provider for the Office of the Secretary of War (OSW), Department of War (DoW) agencies, and offices in the National Capital Region.
MajorDuties: The incumbent serves as a Correspondence Analyst on a rotating shift basis in CAB. Manages all unclassified correspondence and staff action packages coming into and out of the CMD addressed to or from the SecDef, DepSec, and ExecSec ensuring they are analyzed, controlled in CATMS, tasked, suspensed, and routed appropriately to the office of primary responsibility (OPR); dispatched to the required addressees; and archived. Establishes and implements unclassified correspondence procedures for all analysts. Assures priority actions and those of particular interest to the ExecSec are coordinated, staffed, and executed ensuring timely, cohesive, and accurate support. Analyzes incoming correspondence from the President, White House staff, Congress, and foreign officials to determine OPRs, set suspense timelines, and verify correct metadata entry in CATMS for executive tracking. Reconciles the weekly Secretary of Defense Correspondence Action Report (SD 391) to update "stoplight" coordination and monthly performance reports; arbitrates tasking disputes between OSD, Joint Staff, and Military Services. Performs final review of all outgoing correspondence signed by the SecDef, DepSecDef, and ExecSec; coordinates timed releases with the Executive Support Branch and executes dispatch via diplomatic pouch, courier, or secure digital channels. Manages, tasks, and tracks high-priority congressional inquiries and White House referrals, coordinating directly with legislative staff and the Assistant Secretary of War for Legislative Affairs to ensure rapid-response compliance. Serves as the authoritative editor and interpreter of DoD Manual 5110.04-M (Manual for Written Material); conducts quality control audits and administers configuration changes to the CATMS CMD organizational structure.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: The DCIPS occupational structure provides the foundation for managing the DCIPS pay structure. It consists of the following elements: mission categories, occupational groups, and work categories, work levels, pay band (for those DCIPS Components operating under the DCIPS pay banded structure using pay plan IA) and grades (for those DCIPS Components operating under the GG graded structure using pay plan GG), job titles, and competencies. You may qualify at the GG-14 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: Applicant must have directly applicable experience that demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Qualifying experience may have been acquired in any public or private sector job, but will clearly demonstrate past experience in the application of the particular competencies/knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to successfully perform the duties of the position. Such experience is typically in or directly related to the work of the position to be filled. Qualifying experience would be demonstrated by 1) Developing foreign disclosure concepts for inclusion in national and departmental plans and policies; 2) Providing policy support for intelligence sharing and foreign disclosure programs; and 3) Reviewing plans, strategies and proposals supporting foreign disclosure and intelligence sharing activities. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. All qualifications and education requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume. It is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the length of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. Your resume may not exceed two (2) pages. For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the duration of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. Read more about what should I include in my federal resume? at https://www.usajobs.gov/Help/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include/ ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, as part of their application package, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, indicating the service member is otherwise eligible and will be discharged or released within 120 days from the date of submission. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. This "certification" must include your rank, dates of active duty service, type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable), and date any terminal leave will begin. It must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible". Members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if they are on terminal leave.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located in Warfighter Support (WS), Global Partnerships Directorate, Office of the Director for Defense Intelligence (DDI), Office of the Under Secretary of War for Intelligence and Security (OUSW(I&S)). The WS serves as the lead integrator and driver of OUSW(I&S) policy, strategy and guidance for defense policy/strategy, military operations, and foreign partnerships.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Under Secretary of War for Intelligence and Security (OUSW(I&S))
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of War (OSW) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of War in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSW includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of War, Under Secretaries of War, Director of War Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of War, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of War, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: This Position is a Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System (DCIPS) position in the Excepted Service under 10 U.S.C. 1601 If selected, Federal employees currently serving in the competitive service must acknowledge that they will voluntarily leave the competitive service by accepting an offer of employment for a DCIPS excepted service positions. If selected, non-DCIPS candidates must acknowledge that the position they have been selected for is in the excepted service and covered by DCIPS. For more information see https://dcips.defense.gov/ Incumbents typical work assignments may include the following: Develops foreign disclosure concepts on behalf of the Director, GP for inclusion in national and departmental planning documents. Provides authoritative guidance, interpretation, and direction to civilian and military foreign disclosure officials (FDOs) and contractor foreign disclosure representatives (FDRs) assigned to the GP Directorate. Develops and interprets policies and procedures for sharing military intelligence with partner nations. Conducts resources and budget management by preparing and managing budget requests to enhance foreign disclosure and partner engagement capabilities and capacity, including the strategic use of innovative information technology such as artificial intelligence/large language models to support these mission sets.
Details.Education: Education cannot be substituted for experience.
Details.Evaluations: DoD Components with DCIPS positions apply Veterans' Preference to preference eligible candidates as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 USC, in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 2005, DCIPS Employment and Placement. If you are a veteran claiming veterans' preference, as defined by section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must submit documents verifying your eligibility with your application package. Your eligibility and qualifications will be evaluated based on your application materials (e.g., resume, supporting documents), the responses you provide on the application questionnaire, and the result of the USA Hire Competency Based Assessment(s) required for this position (if applicable). If you are found to be among the top candidates, you will be referred to the selecting official for employment consideration. You will be assessed on the following competencies (knowledge, skills, abilities, and other characteristics): Accountability Attention to Detail Customer Service Decision Making Flexibility Influencing/Negotiating Integrity/Honesty Interpersonal Skills Learning Reading Comprehension Reasoning Self-Management Stress Tolerance Teamwork This USA Hire Assessment includes a cut score based on the minimum level of required proficiency in these critical general competencies. You must meet or exceed the cut score to be considered. You will not be considered for the position if you score below the cut score or fail to complete the assessment. Follow the prompts to select your resume and/or other supporting documents to be included with your application package. Your resume cannot exceed two pages. See the Required Documents section above for more information. You will have the opportunity to upload additional documents to include in your application before it is submitted. Your uploaded documents may take several hours to clear the virus scan process, and it is your responsibility to ensure that they do so successfully. After acknowledging you have reviewed your application package, complete the Include Personal Information section as you deem appropriate and click to continue with the application process. The notification will be provided in your application submission screen and via email. The notification will include your unique assessment access link to the USA Hire system and the completion deadline. Do not email or send hard copy resumes/applications to the Contact Information or Agency Information listed in this vacancy announcement. All resumes/applications received at the addresses listed in the Contact Information or Agency Information will be destroyed and will not be considered for this vacancy announcement. It is the applicant's responsibility to verify that all information in their resume and documents are legible and accurate. HR will not modify answers/documents submitted by an applicant.

You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. 10-Point Other Veterans’ Rating 30 Percent or More Disabled Veterans 5-Point Veterans' Preference Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 People with Disabilities, Schedule A Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Reserve (MR) and National Guard (NG) Technician Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD MR and NG Preference Eligible Tech Receiving Disability Retirement Priority Placement Program, DoD Retained Grade Preference Eligible Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998 In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Attention to Detail Customer Service Decision Making Flexibility Influencing/Negotiating Integrity/Honesty Interpersonal Skills Learning Reasoning Self-Management Stress Tolerance Teamwork Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1) Evaluating and advising senior leadership on national-level water resources policies and legislative proposals; 2) Leading coordination efforts for complex issues with high level officials across federal agencies; 3) Drafting executive -level briefs, congressional testimony, formal correspondence and official policy guidance for senior agency leadership; 4) Providing technical or policy recommendations on controversial permit decisions. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-14). Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-14).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serves as an ASSISTANT FOR ENVIRONMENTAL AND REGULATORY AFFAIRS for the Assistant Secretary of the Army (Civil Works).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Assistant Security of the Army (Civil Works) ASA (CW) reports to the SECARMY and serves as the principal advisor to the SECARMY for the Army's Civil Works Program. The ASA (CW) provides oversight of the PPBE process as well as strategic communications for the Army's Civil Works program. The ASA (CW) sets the strategic direction and oversees all matters related to all aspects of the United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Civil Works program, which is executed by the Commander, USACE. Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army.
MajorDuties: Independently reviews and analyzes policies and programs to ensure they align with administration policy and sound technical practices.
Provides authoritative consultation, advice, and policy interpretation to the Assistant Secretary of the Army (Civil Works), the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and other federal agencies.
Identifies problem areas and initiates measures, including proposed legislation and regulation changes, to improve water resources and regulatory programs.

Provides executive direction to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers for developing regulations and policies for compliance with the Administrative Procedure Act, the Clean Water Act, and various Water Resource Development Acts.
Represents the Assistant Secretary of the Army (Civil Works) in contacts with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, other federal agencies, and the public.
Answers formal and informal inquiries from the Executive Office of the President, Congress, other federal agencies, and the public.
Reviews position and decision documents prepared for signature by the Assistant Secretary of the Army (Civil Works).
Details.Education: Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: IMPORTANT INFORMATION: This Job Opportunity Announcement (JOA) will be used to form a pool of qualified applicants who will be considered for direct hire vacancies as they become available. To learn more about the United States Space Force Mission click here
MajorDuties: The United States Space Force (USSF) Peterson SFB, Colorado Springs, CO is searching for an International & Spectrum Engagement Manager (NH-0346-03, GS 12/13 equivalent). *Position is eligible to be filled at either Peterson Space Force Base Colorado Springs, CO or Los Angeles Space Force Base, El Segundo CA* Description: The US Space Force is seeking a dynamic and strategic leader to manage the enterprise intake process for external stakeholders, focusing on international/allied integration and complex regulatory deconfliction. In this high-impact role, you will serve as the primary liaison guiding foreign partners and commercial entities through the bureaucratic, technical, and regulatory requirements necessary to connect to the US Space Force satellite communication network. You will direct the onboarding intake funnel-framing collaboration through established tiered opportunities such as federated network or industrial partnerships-while standardizing processes to minimize friction and ensure capabilities are technically and administratively aligned before production handoff. To ensure global operational readiness, you will navigate, expedite, and manage long-lead regulatory and spectrum licensing processes required for new antenna providers and global operation centers. This position requires exceptional strategic decision support, analytical acumen, superior time management, and highly polished written and oral communication skills to coordinate seamlessly with host nations, major commands, and international directorates to align allied integration with broader US Space Force strategies. Ideal Candidate: An ideal candidate for this US Space Force position will possess a strong academic foundation, holding a bachelor's degree in international relations, Public Policy, National Security, Engineering, or a business/analytical field, with a master's degree preferred, or equivalent specialized military experience. They must exhibit high proficiency in navigating complex, long-lead licensing requirements, particularly through direct coordination with the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA), Federal Communications Commission (FCC), and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). This role demands robust analytical skills to successfully balance stringent security controls with critical operational timelines. Key Skills and Abilities: 1. Knowledge of the applicable principles, concepts, policies, and laws; functions, programs, and systems applicable to the duties of logistics contracts and program management and material support; sources, responsibilities, and means for providing assistance and advice to resolve logistics contracts and program management problems; and all aspects of logistics contracts and program management support. 2. Knowledge of government and private industry policies and practices related to business management, industrial management, financial systems, technical concepts, and production practices. Ability to gather, analyze, and evaluate a variety of program information, such as commercial business practices, market conditions, offer acceptability, contractor acceptability, contractor responsibility and/or performance to determine acquisition strategy and sources. 3. Knowledge of the missions, roles, functions, organizational structures, and operation of the Department of Defense and entities that govern, interface with, and/or influence management control of proposed and ongoing service contracts. 4. Knowledge of methods of supervision to hold others accountable for measurable high-quality, timely, and cost-effective results. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the functions of a unit and mentor, motivate, and appraise subordinate staff. Determine objectives, make sound, well-informed, and objective decisions, set priorities, cause change, and accomplish organizational goals. 5. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, clearly, concisely, with technical accuracy and to use computers and a variety of software programs and databases, gather and analyze a variety of program information progress. 6. Ability to establish and maintain good relationships with individuals and groups within the office as well as outside the immediate work unit and to be persuasive in representing the best interests of the government when dealing with personnel with highly divergent points of view. 7. Ability to plan, organize, analyze problems, translate complex information, make appropriate judgments, evaluate options, conduct research, summarize results, make appropriate recommendations, and manage critical aspects of service contract requirements as related to the assigned functional area and meet deadlines. Ability to compose and edit contract required correspondence, review and analyze directives, develop and brief service contract program related presentations.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions, Miscellaneous Administration and Program Series 0301. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-12, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes thorough knowledge of National, bi-national, bilateral, and DOD-level strategic guidance and policy documents and Traditional Commander's Activities as they apply to TSC programs and C-TCO activities, planning and processes; thorough knowledge of domestic and international political/military issues. Knowledge of the legal and policy framework relating to DOD TSC activities including treaties and international agreements pertaining to the organizations missions with Mexico. Knowledge of the relationships of the various combatant command missions and organizations and the Federal interagency as they relate to Security Cooperation missions in accordance with the organization and other Federal interagency authorities such as support to the Department of State for international assistance. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in­-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-12 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-13 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of DoD and Combatant command, program goals and objectives, operational events and milestones, and methods of evaluating the effectiveness of planning actions related to actual events; and the relationship of the various organizational entities involved in overall program planning and execution of military operations, exercises and evaluations. Knowledge of international organizations, problems, or other aspects of foreign affairs planning, policy or strategy at Combatant Command or DOD_ level and in foreign relations at the military to military or military to government level. Ability to communicate effectively in Spanish, both orally and in writing. Language proficiency-1 (extremely proficient) and language reading, speaking, listening, and writing proficiency+ 36 (general professional, plus). Knowledge of military command structure, missions, programs and organizational relationships and program goals and objectives, management and organizational techniques, contingency planning, exercises planning and processes for us in a wide variety of analytical evaluations and studies related to command initiatives and engagements. Knowledge of Traditional Commander's Activities program and events. Knowledge of Mexico's customs, culture, and story as well as current issues facing the U.S. and Mexico. Knowledge of bi-national bilateral, Government of Mexico, DOD, and Combatant Command strategic guidance documents relating to TSC. Demonstrated ability to perform strategic analysis of National, DOD, and interagency strategy and policy. Ability to gather, assemble, and analyze facts, draw conclusions, conduct analysis, devise recommended solutions and package the entire process in briefings, apers or reports suitable for senior N-NC leadership use and decision-making. In addition, the work requires considerable inter-personal skills in presenting recommendations to administrative policies and procedures and negotiating solutions to disputed recommendations. Skill to defend ideas and support emerging concepts relating to TSC and C-TCO programs and activities. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT (CONTINUED) Work may require short notice travel away from the normal duty station to locations within and outside of the Continental United States on military or commercial aircraft in accordance with Joint Travel Regulations in performance of temporary duty (TDY). Incumbent may be required to obtain an official passport. This position is designated by the Air Force as a Test Designated Position (TDP) under the Air Force Civilian Drug Testing Program. As a mandatory requirement for employment in this TDP, the incumbent is (A) to refrain from use of illegal drugs and (B) if required, to submit to urinalysis testing. Illegal drug use by employees in sensitive position presents a clear threat to the mission of the Air Force, national security, and public safety. The selectee must sign a statement acknowledging the position occupied is identified as a TDP. This is a KEY position IAW 32 CFR, Part 44 Appendix A and DOW Directive 1200.7. A Key Position is a Federal position that cannot be vacated during a war, national emergency, or mobilization without seriously impairing the capability of the parent Federal Agency to function effectively. Applicants for positions designated as "Key" positions who do not agree to this condition shall not be extended an offer of employment. The employee must be removed from the Ready Reserve and CANNOT become a member of the Ready Reserve while assigned to this position. Employee (not designated as Mission Essential) may be required to report for duty at normal times during hazardous weather conditions when the base is closed or delayed reporting is directed and remain on duty during phased or early release if their presence at the worksite is necessary to support exercises, pre-scheduled conferences, or real-world operations. YA002 = Eligible for situational telework only, including Ad hoc, Emergency, or OPM prescribed "Unscheduled" Telework. This eligibility is separate and distinct from the employee's eligibility. A civilian employee's telework arrangement may be terminated at the discretion of the supervisor or at the employee's request. May be required to perform Battle Roster functions during Exercises, Real-World events, or on an as needed basis to support mission requirements. Battle Roster functions may include but are not limited to the Joint Operations Center (JOC), Future Operations Center (FOC), Future Plans Center (FPC), Joint Logistics Operations Center (JLOC), N&NC Deployment and Distribution Operations Center (NDDOC), Joint Intelligence Operations Center-North (JIOC-N), Joint Cyber Center (JCC), and other tasks as assigned. These duties may require additional duty hours and/or a physical/medical assessment to deploy to alternate duty locations (non-combat) or in-place. The physical/medical assessment is not a pre-employment requirement. This position is Non-Combat Essential (NCE) IAW Section 1580 of title 10, USC, and DOES NOT provide civilian support to combat operations. Duties of this position are to provide support for expeditionary requirements and could be deployed to support emergency operations, humanitarian missions, disaster relief or other expeditionary missions in the continental United States or overseas, that are NOT considered "combat" locations. Employee must meet the medical and suitability requirements of the positions as outlined in DD Form 3207 and sign the DD Form 2365 as a condition of employment. QUALIFICATIONS: In order to qualify, you must meet the SPECIALIZED experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions- Miscellaneous Administration and Program Series (0301) SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-14 (or higher) grade level or equivalent (may have been obtained in the federal service, military, or public sector). Examples of specialized experience include- Expert knowledge of DoW and joint Global Force Management policy, doctrine, guidance, and processes in order to interpret, develop, and apply command-level GFM positions, procedures, and doctrine governing force apportionment, allocation, and assignment; Expert knowledge of U.S. national and departmental strategic guidance (e.g., NSS, NDS, NMS, UCP, GEF, JSCP, GFMAP, GFMIG) and how it drives force management decisions, in order to translate broad strategic direction into executable sourcing recommendations, EXORD inputs, and command policy; Comprehensive knowledge of the missions, roles, functions, and organizational relationships of the Joint Staff, CCMDs, Services, and N/NC components in order to synchronize force requirements, negotiate contested allocations, and resolve complex, multi-command sourcing issues; and Expert knowledge of joint and Service operational planning and deployment processes, and of regional security issues and force capabilities relevant to homeland defense and civil support, in order to ensure GFM solutions are operationally feasible, legally compliant, and aligned with CCDR objectives. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in­-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-14 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-15 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Expert knowledge of the policies, principles, concepts, procedures, techniques, and methodologies governing the DoW; military command structure, mission, and relationship factor to develop, interpret, and influence the execution of DoW operations and exercise planning. Expert knowledge of the mission, roles, functions, organizational structures, and operations of DoW and joint organizations, including DoW security policies and procedures to provide command-level staff guidance on the roles and organization of the Joint Services and DoW agencies as they relate to crisis management. Expert knowledge of U.S. national policy and strategic guidance including the National Security Strategy, National Defense Strategy, National Military Strategy, Unified Command Plan, Guidance for the Employment of the Force, Joint Strategic Campaign Plan, Guidance for the Development of the Force, Global Force Management Allocation Plan (GFMAP), Global Force Management Implementation Guidance, and related national plans to interpret and operationalize GFM requirements. Knowledge of regional security issues and an understanding of regional military force capabilities and functions, including the forces and resources required for a wide variety of military operations, contingencies, and missions to develop operations orders and crisis action plans. Knowledge of Joint and Service operational planning, budgeting, and evaluation processes, management procedures, and GFM and Time-Phased Force and Deployment Data (TPFDD) systems to serve and advise senior staff. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the functions of an organization to meet program requirements and objectives within available resources. Ability to communicate orally and in writing, clearly, concisely, and with technical accuracy, and to influence, justify, defend, and negotiate command positions with senior officials and external stakeholders. NOTE: Qualifications continued in the Additional Information section of this announcement.

MajorDuties: SUMMARY: PRIMARY PURPOSE: To serve as the Senior Technical Advisor (STA) and Subject Matter Expert (SME) for Global Force Management (GFM) in the J3 Operations Directorate, NORAD and USNORTHCOM (N/NC), functioning as a Management Official whose duties require and authorize the incumbent to formulate, determine, or influence the policies of the command in force management, force allocation, and force assignment. The incumbent shapes command-level policy through authoritative technical guidance and department-level interpretation of Department of War (DoW) GFM policy and procedures. In this capacity, the incumbent advocates the policy positions of the Division Chief, the J3 Directors of Operations, the Chief of Staff, Deputy Commander, and Combatant Commander (CCDR) on DoW GFM matters. DUTIES: Serves as the STA and command SME for GFM, providing command-level policy, doctrine, and strategic advice on operational force requirements supporting national-security activities. Executes the command's Global Force Management Allocation Plan (GFMAP) processes for annual enduring rotational allocations, emergent Requests for Forces (RFFs), force sourcing, and force-readiness analysis supporting conventional joint military operations. Plans, integrates, and evaluates Force Management Division programs, internal processes, resources, and work priorities to sustain effective command-wide GFM operations. Manages executive GFM taskers, senior-leader training, decision-support products, and administrative support activities that enable timely and informed command action.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Nation's Logistics Combat Support Agency: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is a U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) agency. DLA provides worldwide logistics support for the missions of the Military Departments and the Unified Combatant Commands under conditions of peace and war. It also provides logistics support to other DoD Components and certain Federal agencies, foreign governments, international organizations, and others as authorized.
MajorDuties: Analyzes demand/supply chain performance critical data across all processes and advises on the probable effects of alternative solutions to supply chain problems.
Functions as a Team Lead, coaches, mentors and facilitates duties of the team.
Generates, monitors, revises, analyzes and evaluates KPIs, metrics and other process performance critical data to ensure demand/supply chain is meeting its performance targets.
Performs capability studies and demand/supply chain evaluation studies, reviews studies performed by internal and external personnel for technical accuracy or applicability.
Ensures the appropriate level of coordination and integration with DLA HQ, DLA Troop Support Command, Business Process Analysts, Process Owners and Demand and Supply Chain Analysts.
Coordinates a team approach of shared responsibilities and commitments to provide improved support to internal/external operations/processes.

Information and required documentation for claiming RGP may be found at the General Applicant Information and Definitions link below. To be eligible as a RGP, you must submit the following supporting documents with your application package: a signed Retained Grade PPP Self-Certification Checklist (DD3145-1 (whs.mil)); a copy of your Notification of Personnel Action (SF-50) effecting the placement in retained grade status; or a copy of the notification letter you received regarding the RIF or classification downgrade.

Drug-Free Workplace Policy The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is committed to maintaining a safe, drug-free workplace. All DLA employees are required to refrain from illegal drug use on and off duty. DLA conducts pre-employment, reasonable suspicion, post-accident, and random drug testing. Applicants tentatively selected for employment in testing designated positions will undergo a urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Refusal to undergo testing or testing positive for illegal drugs will result in withdrawal of the tentative job offer and a six-month denial of employment with DLA from the date of the drug test. Employees in drug testing designated positions are subject to random drug testing. A negative drug test result must be received by HR within 30 calendar days after the EOD (i.e., start date). The selectee's inability successfully pass; or refusal to conduct the test may result in: 1) the tentative or FJO being withdrawn during the recruitment process; or 2) subsequently being removed from Federal service for failure to meet a condition of employment. You may be required to sign a "Drug Test Statement of Understanding" if you are selected for this position. The DLA drug testing panel tests for the following substances: marijuana, cocaine, opiates, heroin, phencyclidine, amphetamines, methamphetamines, fentanyl, norfentanyl, methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), methylenedioxyamphetamine (MDA), and opioids. ADVISORY: Use of cannabidiol (CBD) products may result in a positive drug test for marijuana. DLA employees are subject to Federal law and under Federal law, Marijuana is illegal. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: To qualify for a Customer Account Specialist, your resume and supporting documentation must support:A. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience that equipped you with the particular competencies to successfully perform the duties of the position and is directly in or related to this position. To qualify at the GS-11 level, applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-09 level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service, military, or private sector. To qualify at the GS-12 level, applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service, military or private sector. Applicants must meet eligibility requirements including time-in-grade (General Schedule (GS) positions only), time-after-competitive appointment, minimum qualifications, and any other regulatory requirements by the cut-off/closing date of the announcement. Creditable specialized experience includes: GS-11 Conducting program reviews to evaluate and improve customer support programs. Making business recommendations based on information in reports and metrics. Providing advice to customers and other personnel regarding new/revised policies, practices, and procedures. Recommending improvements to customer service programs. GS-12 Handling emergency customer orders and projecting customer requirements.- Resolving complex issues related to customer billing and collection; and developing corrective measures. Establishing criteria to measure organizational goals. Accomplishing studies and rendering techniques to quantify results. Building customer relationships to improve customer service/satisfaction. B. Education Substitution: Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work. Education must be from a college or university accredited by an organization approved by the U.S. Department of Education. See http://ope.ed.gov/accreditation/Search.aspx. If using education to meet basic qualifications, YOU MUST SUBMIT A TRANSCRIPT as supplemental documentation. To qualify based on educationin lieu of specialized experience, you must possess:GS-11 Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree, or three (3) years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a PhD or equivalent Doctorate degree, or LL.M, if related. Such education must be from an accredited college or university, and must demonstrate the knowledge, skills and abilities to do the work. TRANSCRIPTS MUST BE SUBMITTED. GS-12 Education may not be used in lieu of specialized experience for this grade level. C. Combination: Combinations of successfully completed post-high school education and experience may be used to meet total qualification requirements for the GS-11 grade level ONLY, and may be computed by first determining the applicant's total qualifying experience as a percentage of the experience required for the grade level; then determining the applicant's education as a percentage of the education required for the grade level;and then adding the two percentages. The total percentages must equal at least 100 percent to qualify an applicant for that grade level. Only graduate education in excess of the amount required for the next lower grade level may be used to qualify applicants for positions at grade GS-11. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MajorDuties: Work as a senior team member within a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) Cell or Segment Support team.
Serve as the primary customer-facing point of contact for the entire Order Fulfillment process.
Act as a customer advocate and liaison between DLA, supported military services, and other federal agencies to identify needs, resolve issues, and ensure satisfaction.
Monitor the performance of vendors to ensure timely delivery of materials, collaborating with vendors and acquisition personnel to resolve complex logistical or quality issues.

Actively participate in customer outreach initiatives to assess satisfaction, gather new requirements, and inform customers of new DLA capabilities and ordering procedures.

Such study may have been performed on a full-time or part-time basis. Applicants tentatively selected for employment in testing designated positions will undergo a urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment.
